name: Crocus
grown_as: The Dutch (large-flowered) spring crocus. William's is 'Grand Maître', a large lilac-violet Dutch crocus, so it is drawn violet. ⚠️ CHECK the shade.
habit: Low tufts 8 to 12 cm high in flower: a few grass-like leaves and one or two goblet flowers rising straight from the ground. Leaves lengthen to 20 to 30 cm after flowering. Clumps widen as corms multiply.

leaf.arrangement: Two to four leaves from each corm, upright, wrapped together at the base in white papery sheaths
leaf.outline: Very narrow, 4 to 8 mm wide, 10 cm at flowering and up to 30 cm later, even width
leaf.margin: Smooth, the edges turned under a little
leaf.veins: One clear silvery-white stripe down the middle of the upper side; ridged (keeled) beneath
leaf.surface: Smooth, dark green either side of the white stripe
leaf.colour: Dark green with a white central stripe

flower.form: An upright goblet of six petals, opening to a wide star in sun and closing in dull weather
flower.petals: Six tepals, three outer and three inner, nearly equal, oval and rounded at the tip, joined at the bottom into a long thin white tube that runs down into the ground
flower.colour: Lilac-violet (variety), often darker at the base and veined
flower.centre: Three yellow stamens and a bright orange style split into three frilly branches, standing up in the middle
flower.behind: No green sepals or stalk: the flower rises from a white papery sheath at soil level
flower.carried: Alone, upright, one or two per corm, among the leaves
flower.size: Tepals 3 to 5 cm long; 7 to 9 cm across when wide open

fruit: An oval capsule about 1.5 cm, pushed up on a short stalk to a few centimetres above the soil among the leaves in late spring, opening into three to release round red-brown seeds.
seedling: Not drawn. A single grass-like leaf; three years to flower.
winter: Nothing above ground until the leaf tips show in late January or February.

leaf: a silvery-white stripe down the middle
bloom: six equal rounded tepals in a goblet
three yellow stamens and a frilly orange style in the middle
a long white tube below, no green sepals or flower stalk
bulb: a corm, not a bulb: round and flattened, about 2.5 cm
covered in a brown fibrous net-like skin
one or more pointed shoots on top and roots from a flat base
shoots: narrow leaves with white stripes coming up in a tuft inside white papery sheaths
the flower bud rising from the middle of the tuft
flower: goblet flowers rising straight from the ground with no stalk
grass-like leaves with white stripes, about as tall as the flowers
seedhead: long leaves, now taller than the flowers were
an oval pod raised a few centimetres above the soil among them
dormant: nothing above the soil, or a few yellow leaves

look_alikes: Autumn crocus or meadow saffron (Colchicum) flowers in autumn without leaves and has six stamens; its broad leaves come in spring. Crocus tommasinianus is slimmer and paler, silvery outside. Leaves alone look like grass but the white stripe gives them away.
